highlights.title: Teads (TEAD) Q2 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
highlights.summary: Kiviat stated, "Adjusted EBITDA came below our expected range" due to a "spike in expenses in the back half of the quarter" involving timing of discretionary costs and cloud platform migration.Kostman warned that the Direct Response and SME business is "navigating significant strategic and operational headwinds" due to the "broader adoption of AI summaries" shifting traditional organic referral patterns.Management noted that FX fluctuations, particularly in the Israeli shekel, continue to be a "headwind on costs."SUMMARYManagement reported a divergence in business performance during the second quarter, where a 17% revenue decline was contrasted by significant growth in the Enterprise segment. The company stated that while the legacy Direct Response and SME business is facing industry-wide pressure from AI-driven search changes and page view declines, the Enterprise division is executing on its plan to return to growth. Strategic efforts are focused on expanding Connected TV home screen reach through exclusive manufacturer partnerships and the rollout of the Teads CTV Ensemble suite. Management confirmed a shift in capital allocation toward higher-margin Enterprise solutions and programmatic environments to maximize long-term enterprise value.CEO Kostman highlighted the importance of home screen reach, stating, "Growth is driven by our global home screen leadership position, reaching over 500 million home screens globally."Management launched Teads EngageOS, an AI-powered publisher operating system designed to "unify content and ad inventory to monetize complete reader sessions."CFO Kiviat attributed the EBITDA shortfall partly to "temporary transitionary costs as we migrated cloud platform onto a new provider."

highlights.summary: Pangle is expanding its mediation partnership with ironSource by introducing access for Android developers!Last year, ironSource officially partnered with Pangle to become a mediation partner and offer iOS developers access to the Pangle SDK. highlights.title: MNTN or Vibe: How to Choose Your CTV Platform
highlights.summary: MNTN's model is strongest for TV-native, awareness-first buyers comfortable with a managed workflow. Its managed service structure means decisions about targeting, creative, and inventory run through MNTN's team — with limited transparency into which placements your budget is funding or how to reallocate based on what's working.Vibe is built for large brands that run CTV with the same rigor they apply to paid social and search. Knix syncsKlaviyosegments — lapsed customers, non-purchasers, high-LTV cohorts — directly into Vibe, controls which inventory those segments run on, and verifies results through Northbeam with incrementality testing for iROAS CMO reporting. The output is defensible data, not just good numbers.For enterpriseB2Bteams specifically, Vibe supports account-based marketing workflows that connect to your sales stack. NYXT, an automotive dealership marketing platform, used Vibe for ABM-style CTV targeting and brought cost per lead to $0.85 — against $3.50 on LinkedIn for the same accounts.Enterprise teams reporting to a CFO or board need attribution data they can act on, not just report. When inventory is opaque — you know the campaign ran but not which placements drove results — Northbeam data tells you a conversion happened but can't close the loop back to an optimization decision. Vibe gives full placement transparency alongside the same attribution integrations, so the measurement and the media plan connect.Which platform is better for growth-stage brands?

quick.title: What Is Programmatic Advertising and How Does It Work in 2026
quick.summary: Programmatic advertising is the automated buying and placing of digital ads using software and data, instead of manual deals. It targets specific audiences across websites, apps, video, and connected TV, buying each impression individually in milliseconds based on who will see it. The big shift is from buying ad space to buying audiences, which makes spending precise and easy to scale. Most display, video, and CTV ads you see today are bought this way, as a page loads.What is real-time bidding (RTB)?Real-time bidding is the live auction that powers most programmatic advertising. When someone opens a page with ad space, the publisher sends that impression to an ad exchange, advertisers' platforms check it against their targeting and bid in real time. The exchange picks the winner and the ad loads, in under 100 milliseconds. Advertisers never pick one website; they set rules, and the system buys the matching impressions. It is how billions of ad slots are sold daily.What is the difference between a DSP and an SSP?They sit on opposite sides of the same marketplace. A demand-side platform, or DSP, is the advertiser's tool: it buys ad impressions across many exchanges from one place, using your targeting and budgets. A supply-side platform, or SSP, is the publisher's tool: it offers ad space to many buyers and gets the best price per impression. The exchange is where the two meet. So advertisers buy through a DSP, publishers sell through an SSP, and the exchange connects them.How much does programmatic advertising cost?

quick.title: InMobi Advertising Launches A Conversational AI Agent for Media Buyers | Morningstar
quick.summary: “Agencies have been asking us for direct, self-serve access to InMobi supply since we opened Buyer Hub to curators last year, and this is our answer,” said Kunal Nagpal, Chief Business Officer, InMobi Advertising. “We built the agent so a trader doesn't have to choose between speed and control. It recommends the curation and optimization moves, and the trader still makes the call. That's the model we think holds up as agentic advertising matures, on both the supply side and the demand side.”Buyer Hub debuted in June 2025 as InMobi's self-serve platform for media buyers, with curators live first and agency access promised as the next phase. Since then, a market requirement scoping exercise with agency and Managed Service DSP customers shaped the product now going live, with agency demand for direct portal access as the clearest signal from that process."We see Buyer Hub as a valuable platform for agencies,” said Ricky Lo, Senior Manager, Products & Analytics, PMX, Publicis Media. “Its deal marketplaces make campaign setup more efficient and allow teams to easily activate high-performing inventory. The streamlined activation process is also a strong advantage for trading teams seeking greater efficiency and ease of execution.”Inside Buyer Hub, the agent recommends curation and optimization moves grounded in live campaign context, while traders stay in control of every decision. The platform adds:Role-based access control, giving agencies account-level view and edit permissions mapped to how their teams actually operateInventory discovery, allowing teams to curate InMobi supply before activation without email back-and-forth

quick.title: DSP vs SSP vs DMP: Key Differences and Which One Is for You
quick.summary: According to Fortune Business Insights , the global DSP market alone is projected to grow from $38.92 billion in 2025 to $48.19 billion by the end of 2026, with no signs of slowing. By the way, the show is “DSP vs. SSP,” the theme is about their differences and by the finale you’ll get which is most suitable for you and how to distinguish the good ones from the average. Epom is in the director’s seat; let’s roll! DSP vs SSP: What Is Programmatic Advertising? Before the detailed explanation of what DSP and SSP is, we’ve got to lay out the basics. Both DSP and SSP are not some concepts detached from reality; they are software! And this software is used for something called programmatic advertising . The DSP is made for those who buy ads (later on that), and the SSP is for those who sell their inventory.What’s this programmatic advertising? Think of it as a way to buy & sell ads automatically powered by real-time bidding RTB technology. It came as a successor to direct deals – the type of media buying where advertisers and publishers have to “manually” negotiate prices for each specific ad placement. Nowadays, even direct media buying has come far in terms of automation, but with it DSPs and SSPs programmatic is still the ad king if you want things done fast and with minimal human interference.
